analyzed_vuln.description: `SendBuffered` trusts the send callback’s return value (`sent`) to be <= the requested length, but validates it against the mutable `outputBuffer.length` field that may no longer match the actual allocated/valid contiguous bytes at `buffer + idx` in this DTLS path. In this PoV, DTLS buffering/reallocation leaves `outputBuffer.length` larger than the backing allocation tail from current `idx`, so `SendBuffered` passes an oversized `sz` to `CBIOSend` (`fuzzer_send`), which then reads past heap allocation in `memory_test`/`fwrite`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered in DTLS client handshake (`wolfSSL_connect` -> `ProcessReplyEx` -> `DoDtlsHandShakeMsg`/`DtlsMsgPoolSend`) when crafted input drives output-buffer growth/fragmentation state such that `outputBuffer.length` becomes inconsistent with actual readable bytes from `outputBuffer.buffer + outputBuffer.idx`. Then an alert send path (`SendFatalAlertOnly` -> `SendAlert` -> `SendAlert_ex` -> `SendBuffered`) calls the I/O send callback with this inflated size; the fuzz harness send callback reads `sz` bytes from the pointer, causing heap OOB read.
